title: Minimum Inversion Count in Subarrays of Fixed Length
summary: Given an integer array nums of length n and an integer k, find the minimum number of inversions in any subarray of length k.
statement: Given an integer array nums of length n and an integer k, find the minimum number of inversions in any subarray of length k.
constraints: nums contains up to 100,000 positive integers and 1≤k≤n.
An inversion in a window is a pair i<j with nums[i]>nums[j].
Return the minimum inversion count among all contiguous length-k windows.
hints: Maintain the current window’s value frequencies in a Fenwick tree.
When removing its leftmost value, subtract remaining values smaller than it; when appending on the right, add existing values greater than it.
Coordinate-compress values, update both changes in logarithmic time, and track the minimum.
These are exactly the inversion pairs incident to the departing and arriving endpoints; all other pairs persist.
editorial: These are exactly the inversion pairs incident to the departing and arriving endpoints; all other pairs persist.

tests.explanation: The middle window [1,2,5] has zero inversions.
The only window is fully decreasing and has six inversions.
